summary: Count by ones and tens to 100 and beyond, and keep counting on from any starting number.
Write numerals 0 to 20, read number words to ten, and match a numeral to a set.
Count objects one-to-one, know the last number tells how many, and count out 1 to 20 objects.
Tell how many are in a patterned group of up to 10 objects without counting.
Decide whether one group has more, fewer or the same number of objects as another.
Compare two written numbers from 1 to 20.
Know ten as a group of ten ones; show numbers 10 to 20 as tens and ones.
Solve everyday adding and subtracting problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Break numbers below 10 into pairs in different ways with objects or drawings and name matching equations.
Find the number that makes 10 with any number from 1 to 9 and record it.
Make, extend and state the rule for simple repeating and growing patterns of numbers and shapes.
Compare flat and solid shapes of any size or orientation by their parts and features.
Directly compare objects by length, capacity, weight and temperature using words like longer or heavier.
Use time words like morning, yesterday, week and year; know clocks and calendars measure time.
With help, sort data into simple bar graphs, picture graphs or tables and compare the groups.
Count to 120 or more by ones, fives and tens from any number; read and write numerals.
Model two-digit numbers as tens and ones, including multiples of ten, with objects and drawings.
Match ordinal words like first, second and third to positions in a line of up to 20.
Compare two two-digit numbers by their tens and ones and record with >, = or <.
Know addition and subtraction facts within 20 fluently using strategies; model zero and the equal sign.
Solve add-to, take-from, put-together, take-apart and compare problems within 20 with unknowns anywhere.
Add within 100, including two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of ten, and explain the strategy.
Make, extend and describe the rule for number patterns built by adding within 100.
Tell defining from non-defining features of flat and solid shapes, and draw shapes with given features.
Put flat or solid shapes together to make a composite shape, then build new shapes from it.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths and describe the parts and the whole.
Compare and order objects by length, area, capacity, weight and temperature directly or with non-standard units.
Tell time to the half hour on analog clocks, relate times to events, and read digital clocks.
Know the value of a penny, nickel and dime and of small collections of them.
Collect survey data, show it in simple bar graphs, picture graphs or tables, and draw conclusions.
Count by ones, twos, fives, tens and hundreds from any number up to at least 1,000.
Read and write numbers to 1,000 in words, models, standard form and expanded form.
Tell whether a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even by pairing or splitting it.
Know a hundred as ten tens; model three-digit numbers as hundreds, tens and ones.
Compare two three-digit numbers by place value and record with >, = or <.
Solve add and subtract word problems within 100 with unknowns anywhere; estimate to check sums.
Add and subtract within 1,000 using place value strategies, regrouping when needed, and explain why.
Show that changing the order or grouping of addends does not change the sum.
Make, extend and describe the rule for number patterns using adding and subtracting within 1,000.
Identify, describe and sort flat and solid shapes by faces, sides and corners; draw flat shapes.
Explore and predict what happens when flat and solid shapes are put together or taken apart.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal parts need not match in shape.
Describe how inches, feet and yards relate, and how centimeters relate to meters.
Estimate and measure length with rulers, yardsticks and tapes to the nearest inch, foot, yard, cm or m.
Estimate and measure capacity in cups and pints; add and subtract to solve capacity problems.
Tell time to five minutes with a.m. and p.m.; add and subtract hour and half-hour intervals.
Know how seconds, minutes, hours, days, weeks, months and years relate to one another.
Find the total value of a set of pennies, nickels, dimes, quarters and dollar bills.
Collect data, show it in bar and picture graphs scaled by 2, 5, 10 or 100, and interpret it.
Read and write whole numbers to 10,000 in words, models, standard form and expanded form.
Model a unit fraction as one equal part of a whole, and other fractions as several unit parts.
Place a fraction on a number line by marking off equal unit-fraction lengths from zero.
Use fraction models to show and make simple equivalent fractions like 1/2 = 2/4.
Compare two fractions with the same top or bottom number and record with >, = or <.
Use place value to round 2- and 3-digit numbers to the closest ten or hundred.
Add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers fluently with place-value strategies and algorithms.
Solve real-world problems that add and subtract multi-digit whole numbers, using equations with an unknown.
Model multiplication as equal groups, arrays, areas and number-line jumps; show what multiplying by 0 and 1 does.
Model division as sharing, partitioning and the inverse of multiplication; show dividing with 0 and 1.
Multiply and divide within 100 using fact families and properties of operations.
Know all multiplication facts and related division facts for 0 through 10 fluently.
Solve multiplication and division word problems within 100 about equal groups, arrays and measures.
Make, extend and state the rule for number patterns within 100, including in addition and times tables.
Recognize rhombuses, rectangles and squares as quadrilaterals; draw examples and non-examples.
Identify and draw points, lines and line segments with tools, and use them to describe shapes.
Split shapes into parts of equal area and name each part as a unit fraction.
Estimate and measure mass in grams and kilograms and volume in quarts, gallons and liters; solve problems.
Measure length to the quarter inch, weight in pounds, and temperature in Celsius and Fahrenheit.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in minutes, e.g. on a number line.
Count any mix of coins and bills, write amounts with cents or dollar signs, and check affordability.
Find rectangle area by tiling and by multiplying sides; draw rectangles sharing area or perimeter.
Find the perimeter of polygons, including when one side length is unknown.
Collect data, show it in scaled bar and picture graphs, and solve problems using the graphs.
Read and write whole numbers to 1,000,000 in words, models, standard form and expanded form.
Model mixed numbers and improper fractions, and whole numbers written as fractions, on number lines and areas.
Use fraction models to explain and generate equivalent fractions.
Compare fractions with unlike numerators and denominators using common parts or benchmarks; record with symbols.
Write tenths and hundredths as fractions and decimals, in expanded form; know decimal forms of halves and fourths.
Compare two decimals to hundredths and record with >, = or <.
Use place value to round large whole numbers to a chosen place.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit and two digits by two digits with place-value strategies.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders, using place-value strategies.
Use the commutative, associative and distributive properties of multiplication.
Find factors and multiples of whole numbers up to 100.
Solve multiplicative comparison word problems and tell them apart from additive comparisons.
Add and subtract like-denominator fractions with models; break fractions into sums of unit fractions.
Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators.
Solve word problems adding and subtracting fractions with like denominators.
Generate a number pattern from a rule and describe how its terms relate.
Identify, describe and draw parallelograms, rhombuses and trapezoids with a ruler or other tools.
Identify and draw rays, right, acute and obtuse angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Classify triangles and quadrilaterals by parallel or perpendicular sides and by angle type.
Measure lengths precisely, to 1/4 or 1/8 of an inch or to the millimeter.
Rewrite metric, customary and time measures in smaller units of the same system; solve problems.
Solve word problems about distance, time, volume, mass and money, including simple fractions and unit changes.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles; find areas of shapes made of rectangles.
Pose data questions; collect data and show it in line plots, bar graphs and frequency tables.
Make a line plot of measurements in halves, fourths and eighths and solve problems from it.
Use a number line to put fractions, mixed numbers and thousandths decimals in order.
Explain a fraction as part of a whole, part of a set, or a whole number divided by another.
Explain zero and decimal-point patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10; use exponents.
Model percents as parts of 100 with pictures and find the equal fraction.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit numbers, with remainders, and explain the strategy.
Solve multiplication and division word problems, explaining how any remainder affects the answer.
Add and subtract fractions or mixed numbers whose denominators differ, by strategy or algorithm.
Solve word problems adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators; estimate to check answers.
Multiply fractions by fractions or whole numbers, using area or other fraction pictures.
Divide fractions by whole numbers or by other fractions, using pictures and numbers.
Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Solve real-world problems dividing fractions and mixed numbers.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and place-value strategies.
Solve real-world decimal problems with all four operations, including money.
Graph points in the first quadrant to show real-world problems and interpret the coordinates.
Identify and draw right, acute and obtuse triangles and circles; relate radius and diameter.
Convert between units within one measurement system and use this in multi-step problems.
Find the area of a rectangle with fraction side lengths by tiling and by multiplying.
Develop and use area formulas for triangles, parallelograms and trapezoids; solve area and perimeter problems.
Find a rectangular prism's volume by packing unit cubes and by multiplying edges or base times height.
Use the formulas length x width x height and base x height for prism volume problems.
Pose data questions, predict, then collect and graph data in fraction line plots, histograms or other displays.
Find mean, median and mode of a data set and choose which best describes it.

state_code: # SOURCES (Indiana Academic Standards for Mathematics, adopted by the Indiana SBOE June 2023; taught from 2024-25; assessed by ILEARN from 2025-26)
# - The 122 K-5 codes match between the standards PDFs and the correlation guides. Process standards PS.1-PS.8 are skipped.
# STRANDS (Indiana calls them domains; code = grade.STRAND.number, numbered without gaps)
# - NS = Number Sense; CA = Computation and Algebraic Thinking; G = Geometry; M = Measurement; DA = Data Analysis
# - "(E)" in the official text marks standards IDOE designates as essential; that flag is not carried here.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED (not covered by any 2023 IAS K-5 standard)
# - K.CC.B.4c (each next number is one more), K.OA.A.5 (fluency within 5), K.G.A.1, K.G.A.2, K.G.A.3, K.G.B.5, K.G.B.6 (Kindergarten geometry cut to one standard)
# - 1.OA.A.2 (three addends), 1.OA.B.4, 1.OA.C.5, 1.OA.D.8 (unknown in an equation), 1.NBT.C.5 (10 more/less mentally), 1.NBT.C.6 (subtract multiples of 10)
# - 2.OA.C.4 (arrays as repeated addition), 2.NBT.B.5 (fluency within 100), 2.NBT.B.6 (add up to four 2-digit numbers), 2.NBT.B.8 (+/-10 or 100 mentally),
# - 3.OA.A.4 (unknown factor), 3.NBT.A.3 (times multiples of 10), 3.NF.A.3c (whole numbers as fractions, now IN 4.NS.2); line-plot part of 3.MD.B.4
# - 4.OA.A.1, 4.NBT.A.1 (place value ten times), 4.NF.C.5 (tenths to hundredths), 4.MD.C.5, 4.MD.C.6, 4.MD.C.7 (angle measure, protractor), 4.G.A.3 (symmetry);
#   5.NBT.B.5 (standard algorithm for multi-digit multiplication), 5.NF.B.5 (multiplication as scaling), 5.G.B.3, 5.G.B.4 (shape hierarchy)
# - Patterns: K.CA.4, 1.CA.4, 2.CA.4 (rule-based number/shape patterns; marked new).
# - Subitizing to 10 (K.NS.4), ordinal numbers (1.NS.3), time vocabulary/calendar (K.M.2), time-unit relationships (2.M.5).
# - Money in grades 1-3: 1.M.3 coins, 2.M.6, 3.M.4 coins and bills with $/cents (marked moved/edited against 2.MD.C.8).
# - Customary capacity in grade 2 (2.M.3 cups/pints) and unit relationships in grade 2 (2.M.1; CCSS 4.MD.A.1).
# - Quadrilateral types drawn with tools (4.G.1), measuring to 1/8 inch and mm (4.M.1), triangles by angle and circles/radius/diameter (5.G.1).
# - Grade 6 CCSS content in grade 5 (no K-5 CCSS code, so marked new with empty ccss): percents (5.NS.4, ~6.RP.A.3c),
#   area of triangles/parallelograms/trapezoids (5.M.3, ~6.G.A.1), mean/median/mode (5.DA.2, ~6.SP.B.5c); 5.CA.6 adds fraction-by-fraction division (~6.NS.A.1).
# UNCERTAIN / JUDGEMENT CALLS (IDOE guide gives no CCSS link, or I added one)
# - Added links not in the IDOE guide: K.NS.3 +K.CC.B.5 (count out 1-20), K.CA.1 +K.OA.A.1, K.DA.1 -> K.MD.B.3, 1.CA.1 +2.OA.B.2 (fluency within 20 is CCSS grade 2),
# - "moved" without an IDOE link: 1.M.3 and 3.M.4 (money, 2.MD.C.8), 2.M.1 (4.MD.A.1), 2.M.3 (3.MD.A.2 liquid volume), 4.CA.3 (3.OA.B.5 properties), 4.DA.1 (3.MD.B.3),
# - Kept as new (no fair CCSS match): 2.G.2 (predict composing/decomposing shapes; near 1.G.A.2), 4.G.1, 4.M.1.
